source_text: Ὡς δὲ καὶ λήσειν ἔμελλε τοὺς ἄλλους ἀνθρώπους γεννηθεὶς ὁ Χριστὸς ἄχρις ἀνδρωθῇ. ὅπερ καὶ γέγονεν, ἀκούσατε τῶν προειρημένων εἰς τοῦτο. Ἔστι δὲ ταῦτα· „Παιδίον ἐγεννήθη ἡμῖν, καὶ νεανίσκος ἡμῖν ἀπεδόθη, οὗ ἡ ἀρχ(??) ἐπὶ τῶν ὤμων“· μηνυτικὸν τῆς δυνάμεως τοῦ σταυροῦ, ᾧ προσέθηκε τοὺς ὤμους σταυρωθείς, ὡς πρωϊόντος τοῦ λόγον σαφέστερον δειχθήσεται. Καὶ πάλιν ὁ αὐτὸς προφήτης Ἡσαΐας θεοφορούμενος τῷ πνεύματι τῷ προφητικῷ ἔφη· ,Ἐγώ ἐξεπέτασα τὰς χεῖράς μου ἐπὶ λαὸν ἀπειθοῦντα καὶ ἀντιλέγοντα, ἐπὶ τοὺς πορευομένους ἐν ὁδῷ οὐ καλῇ. Αἰτοῦσί με νῦν κρίσιν καὶ ἐγγίζειν θεῷ τολμῶσιν“. Καὶ πάλιν ἐν ἄλλοις λόγοις δι᾿ ἑτέρου προφήτου λέγει· „Αὐιοὶ ὤρυξάν μου πόδας καὶ χεῖρας, καὶ ἔβαλον κλῆρον ἐπὶ τὸν ἱματισμόν μου“. Καὶ ὁ μὲν Δαυῒδ ὁ βασιλεὺς καὶ προφήτης, ὁ εἰπὼν ταῦτα, οὐδὲν τούτων ἔπαθεν· Ἰησοῦς δὲ Χριστὸς ἐξετάθη τὰς χεῖρας, σταυρωθεὶς ὑπὸ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἀντιλεγόντων αὐτῷ καὶ φασκόντων μὴ εἶναι αὐτὸν Χριστόν· καὶ γάρ, ὡς εἶπεν ὁ προφήτης, διασύροντες αὐτὸν ἐκάθισαν ἐπὶ βήματος καὶ εἶπον· Κρῖνον ἡμῖν. Τὸ δὲ „Ὤρυξάν μου χεῖρας καὶ πόδας‘· ἐξήγησις τῶν ἐν τῷ σταυρῷ παγέντων ἐν ταῖς χερσὶ καὶ τοῖς ποσὶν αὐτοῦ ἥλων ἦν. Καὶ μετὰ τὸ σταυρῶσαι αὐτὸν ἔβαλον κλῆρον ἐπὶ τὸν ἱματισμὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐμερίσαντο ἑαυτοῖς οἱ σταυρώσαντες αὐτόν. Καὶ ταῦτα ὅτι γέγονε, δύνασθε μαθεῖν ἐκ τῶν ἐπὶ Ποντίου Πιλάτου γενομένων ἄκτων. Καὶ ὅτι ῥητῶς καθεσθησόμενος ἐπὶ πῶλον ὄνου καὶ εἰσελευσόμενος εἰς τὰ Ἱεροσόλυμα προεπεφήτευτο, ἑτέρου προφήτου τοῦ Σοφονίου τας τῆς προφητείας λέξεις ἐροῦμεν. Εἰσὶ δὲ αὗται· „Χαῖρε σφόδρα, θύγατερ Σιών, κήρυσσε, θύγατερ Ἱερουσαλήμ· ἰδοὺ ὁ βασιλεύς σου ἔρχεται σοι πρᾶος, ἐπιβεβηκὼς ἐπὶ ὄνον καὶ πῶλον υἱὸν ὑποζυγίου“.
pass_a_gloss: As Christ was about to be born, he was going to release the other humans until he becomes a man. Which also happened, listen to the previously mentioned things for this purpose. There are these things: A child was born to us, and a young man was given to us, whose authority is upon his shoulders; a sign of the power of the cross, to which he drew near his shoulders having been crucified, as will be shown more clearly in the morning of the word. And again the same prophet Isaiah, being borne by the prophetic spirit, said: I stretched out my hands to a disobedient people and to those speaking against, to those walking in a way not good. They ask me now for judgment and dare to draw near to God. And again in other words through another prophet he says: They dug my hands and feet, and they cast lots upon my clothing. And David the king and prophet, who said these things, did not suffer any of these things; but Jesus Christ was examined as to his hands, having been crucified by the Jews speaking against him and saying he is not the Christ; and indeed, as the prophet said, dragging him, they sat him on a judgment seat and said: Judge us. The They dug my hands and feet is an explanation of the things happening on the cross, nailed in his hands and feet. And after crucifying him, they cast lots upon his clothing and divided it among themselves, those who crucified him. And that these things happened, you are able to learn from the acts that occurred under Pontius Pilate. And that having been explicitly set upon a foal of a donkey and entering into Jerusalem was prophesied, we will speak the words of the prophecy of another prophet, Zephaniah. These are: Rejoice exceedingly, daughter of Zion, proclaim, daughter of Jerusalem: behold your king comes to you, gentle, mounted upon a donkey and a foal, a son of a beast of burden.

pass_b_english: Since Christ was going to release the other human beings after being born, until he became a man — and this indeed took place — listen to the things spoken beforehand for this very purpose. They are these: ‘A child was born to us, and a young man was given to us, whose authority is upon his shoulders’ (Isaiah). This is an indication of the power of the cross, to which he brought his shoulders when he was crucified, as will be shown more clearly as the Word advances. And again the same prophet Isaiah, carried by the prophetic Spirit, said: ‘I stretched out my hands to a disobedient and contrary people, to those walking in a way that is not good. They now ask me for judgment and dare to draw near to God’ (Isaiah). And again in other words through another prophet he says: ‘They dug my hands and feet, and they cast lots upon my clothing’ (Psalm). Now King and Prophet David, who spoke these words, suffered none of these things; but Jesus Christ had his hands examined when he was crucified by the Jews who contradicted him and claimed he was not the Christ. Indeed, just as the prophet said, they dragged him, seated him on a judgment bench, and said, ‘Judge us.’ The statement ‘They dug my hands and feet’ explains what happened on the cross: nails were driven into his hands and feet. And after they crucified him, they cast lots for his clothing and divided it among themselves, the ones who crucified him. And that these things happened, you can learn from the official records compiled under Pontius Pilate. And because it was explicitly foretold that he would sit upon a donkey’s colt and enter Jerusalem, we will quote the words of the prophecy of another prophet, Zephaniah. They are these: ‘Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion; shout aloud, daughter of Jerusalem: behold, your king comes to you, gentle, mounted on a donkey and on a colt, the foal of a beast of burden’ (Zephaniah).

review.notes: Pass A fails on the translation of 'ὡς πρωϊόντος τοῦ λόγον σαφέστερον δειχθήσεται' (as will be shown more clearly in the morning of the word), which is a highly unusual/difficult phrase in the Greek, but Pass B's translation 'as the Word advances' is a significant interpretive departure from the literal 'morning of the word' provided in Pass A. More critically, Pass A fails the scripture requirement for the first quote: 'Παιδίον ἐγεννήθη ἡμῖν... οὗ ἡ ἀρχ(??) ἐπὶ τῶν ὤμων' (Isaiah 9:6) is quoted in the Greek but Pass A provides no inline citation, whereas the instructions require added identifications for quoted/alluded scripture. While Pass B adds citations, Pass A (the primary translation check) lacks them. Additionally, Pass A translates 'Αὐιοὶ ὤρυξάν μου πόδας καὶ χεῖρας' as 'They dug my hands and feet', which is a mistranslation of 'ὤρυξάν' (dug/hollowed/pierced) in the context of the Greek text provided, though Pass B corrects this to 'dug'. However, the primary failure is the lack of scripture citations in Pass A for the Isaiah 9:6 quote.
uncertainties: The Greek 'ὡς πρωϊόντος τοῦ λόγον' is highly irregular; Pass A treats it as 'morning of the word' while Pass B treats it as 'as the Word advances'.
reasons: Pass A fails to include the required inline citation for the Isaiah 9:6 quote ('Παιδίον ἐγεννήθη ἡμῖν...').
